on "the book of base rates" (Mauboussin), u want to keep these tables somewhere within arm's reach

especially at first when u aren't sure where the bounded universe ends

this helps with ur own forecasts, and with knowing when someone else is making a ridiculous assumption

below, u can see that for a sales CAGR of 30-35%

on a 1-yr basis, only 2% of companies were able to sustain that growth rate 

and on a 10-year basis, that falls to 0.5% of companies.

but you will still see and hear tons of wacky forecasts where some company is projecting a 50% 5-10 year CAGR. there's tables for earnings growth in there as well

for something like n=5 anything can happen, but over 10,000 reps, reality is going to map to these odds

there's always some stupid fad business where mgmt throws out a number, and u check the book of base rates, and u realize the % growth rate is higher than Google

meanwhile the company is a fuckin grocery store, or they send u dog food in the mail, or sell furniture over the internet

the book of base rates will always be ur friend when it comes to either avoiding nonsense, or just adding support around the rest of ur assumptions.
